fact: People who have frequent nightmares often remember far more detail from their dreams than other dreamers.
body:
People who regularly experience nightmares often recall their dreams with an unusually high level of detail — faces, sounds, feelings, even smells.

That is no coincidence. Nightmares strongly activate the limbic system, especially the amygdala — the brain's fear center. This emotional intensity anchors dreams more deeply in memory. It's the same mechanism that makes us remember emotionally charged experiences from waking life more vividly.

People who have nightmares often are, in a sense, training their mind to hold on to dream images. That also explains why many people with vivid nightmares report feeling stuck as if in a film — the dream feels real because the brain treats it like a genuine memory.

The good news: this ability to recall dreams in such detail is also a strength. Those who write down and understand their dreams often find valuable clues about what their subconscious is processing.
